intro: The rooms of a house and its furniture. Today you learn to say what a house has and what there is in each room.
b1.texto:
To talk about a house, two very common verbs are used:

- **tener**, when the subject is the house or a person: «Mi piso **tiene** un salón».
- **hay**, when you say what exists in a place: «En el salón **hay** un sofá».

Notice the difference: «El piso **tiene** dos dormitorios» and «En el piso **hay** dos dormitorios». Both sentences are correct, but you don't say «el piso hay».
b2.f2.texto: It has a living room, a kitchen and a bedroom.
b2.f4.texto: No, but there is a window in the living room.
b2.f5.texto: The television is in front of the sofa.
b4.texto:
To say where a piece of furniture is, use these expressions:

- **delante de** (in front of): «La televisión está delante del sofá».
- **detrás de** (behind): «La lavadora está detrás de la puerta».
- **al lado de** (next to): «La lámpara está al lado de la cama».
- **dentro de** (inside): «Los platos están dentro del armario».

They all take **de**, and with «el» they merge: de + el = **del**.
b4.e0.texto: The flat has a living room.
b4.e1.texto: There is a sofa in the living room.
b5.f0.texto: Lucía lives in a small flat.
b5.f1.texto: The flat has a living room, a kitchen and a bedroom.
b5.f2.texto: In the living room there is a sofa and a window.
b5.f3.texto: The kitchen is small, but it has a new fridge.
b5.f4.texto: In the bedroom there is a bed and a wardrobe.
b5.f5.texto: Lucía loves her flat very much.
b6.pregunta: What is there in the living room?
b6.o0.refuerzo: Correct: the living room has a sofa and a window.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The bed is in the bedroom.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The fridge is in the kitchen.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Correct: the subject is «el piso», so «tiene» is the one that fits.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Incorrect: «hay» takes no subject. You would say «en el piso hay un salón».
b7.o2.refuerzo: Incorrect: «está» is used to say where something is, not to say that something has something.
b8.traduccion: There is a sofa in the living room.
b8.frase: En el salón hay un sofá.
b9.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «The flat is small».
p.el piso.consejo: In Spain you say «piso»; in Latin America, «apartamento» or «departamento».
p.el salón.consejo: It has an accent on the «o»: sa-LON.
p.la cocina.consejo: The first «c» is a «k» and the second one sounds «th» in Spain: ko-THI-na.
p.el dormitorio.consejo: You can also say «la habitación», the room.
p.el sofá.consejo: It has an accent on the final «á» and it is masculine: «el sofá».
p.la cama.consejo: «Estar en la cama» is the usual way to say someone is lying down or resting in bed.
p.el armario.consejo: The «r» is soft, a single tap: ar-MA-ryo.
p.la lámpara.consejo: The accent goes on the first «a»: LAM-pa-ra.
p.la ventana.consejo: The «v» is pronounced like a soft «b»: ben-TA-na.
p.delante de.consejo: It always goes with «de»: «delante del sofá».
p.detrás de.consejo: It has an accent on the «a»: de-TRAS. And you say «detrás del», not «detrás el».
p.salón.consejo: The accent on «ó» shows the stress is on the last syllable. In the plural it disappears: «salones».
p.delante.consejo: It usually goes with «de»: «delante del sofá». Its opposite is «detrás», behind.
p.sofá.consejo: The accent on «á» shows the stress is on the last syllable: so-FA. The plural is «sofás».
p.nevera.consejo: It is related to «nieve», snow, because it keeps things cold. The «v» sounds like «b»: ne-BE-ra.
p.cama.consejo: A «cama» is where you sleep. It is in the «dormitorio». Plural: «camas».
p.armario.consejo: It is the big piece of furniture for clothes. The «io» glides into one syllable: ar-MA-ryo.
p.televisión.consejo: The accent on «ó» marks the last syllable: te-le-bi-SYON. It is feminine, «la televisión», and the «v» sounds like «b».
